ceo_directive: Pre-register the cheapest experiment that could prove us wrong. Do not tune the design to pass thresholds after seeing results.
principle: A model that survives has earned an experiment, not a victory. The experiment's job is to try to KILL R6, not to confirm it.

experiments.name: Valve opening pressure and tolerance
experiments.hypothesis: The passive bypass valve opens at 20-25 mmHg with <5 mmHg tolerance
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 5: manufacturing tolerance ±5% per dimension → ±7.5 mmHg pressure variation → EXCEEDS ±5 mmHg tolerance
apparatus: Dual-lumen catheter prototype with passive slit valve (silicone, injection-molded)
Pressure-controlled water column (0-50 mmHg, calibrated manometer ±0.5 mmHg)

parameters.valve_design: slit valve in silicone catheter wall

experiments.measurement: For each valve: ramp pressure from 0 to 50 mmHg in 1 mmHg steps. Record the pressure at which flow first exceeds 0.01 mL/min (= opening pressure). Record flow at each pressure point.

threshold.tolerance_mmhg: ±5 mmHg (i.e., 95% of valves must open between 15 and 30 mmHg)

experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if >1 of 20 valves opens outside 15-30 mmHg range, OR if median opening pressure is outside 20-25 mmHg, OR if flow at 25 mmHg < 0.05 mL/min for any valve.
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all 20 valves. Do not stop early. Report all results including failures. No post-hoc exclusion of outliers.

experiments.name: Bypass flow measurement at obstruction pressure
experiments.hypothesis: Bypass flow at 25 mmHg ≥ 0.35 mL/min (meets CSF production rate)
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 8: Poiseuille equation predicts 1.53 mL/min, but this assumes ideal laminar flow, no entrance effects, no valve resistance. Real flow may be 50-80% lower.
apparatus: Collection vessel on analytical balance (±0.001 g) for gravimetric verification
experiments.measurement: For each valve: apply constant 25 mmHg pressure. Measure flow rate at 1, 5, and 10 minutes. Record steady-state flow (average of minutes 5-10). Weigh collected fluid for gravimetric verification.
experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if median steady-state flow < 0.35 mL/min (insufficient to match CSF production → ICP continues rising). CONDITIONAL_FAIL if flow 0.35-1.0 mL/min (partial drainage, need to re-evaluate time-to-herniation). PASS if flow ≥ 1.0 mL/min.
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all 10 valves × 5 trials. Report all results.

experiments.name: Drainage under valve failure-open conditions
experiments.hypothesis: Bypass flow at normal ICP (15 mmHg) < 10% of primary flow
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 1: if valve fails open, 6.2% over-drainage predicted. Need to verify this is actually < 10%.
apparatus: Prototype with valve intentionally locked open (failure-open simulation)
experiments.measurement: Measure primary flow and bypass flow simultaneously at 15 mmHg with valve forced open. Calculate bypass/primary ratio.
experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if bypass/primary ratio > 10% at normal ICP (chronic over-drainage risk exceeds obstruction-prevention benefit). CONDITIONAL_FAIL if 5-10% (marginal). PASS if < 5%.
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all 5 prototypes × 3 trials. Report all results.

experiments.name: Bypass engagement at partial obstruction levels
experiments.hypothesis: Bypass opens when primary lumen radius is reduced by ≥12%
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 3: model predicts 12% radius reduction triggers bypass. Need to verify the ICP-pressure relationship experimentally.
apparatus: Prototype with adjustable primary lumen obstruction (tapered plug, 0-100%)
Pressure transducer at proximal end (±0.5 mmHg)
experiments.measurement: At each obstruction level: measure ICP, primary flow, and bypass flow. Record the obstruction level at which bypass first activates (flow > 0.01 mL/min).
experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if bypass does not activate until >20% obstruction (sub-threshold window too large — symptomatic hydrocephalus  untreated). PASS if activates at ≤15% obstruction.
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all levels. Report the full activation curve.

experiments.name: Common-mode failure: simultaneous obstruction of both lumens
experiments.hypothesis: Spatially offset outlets prevent simultaneous obstruction
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 4: if outlets are co-located, tissue ingrowth covers both. Need to test whether offset actually prevents common-mode failure.
apparatus: Prototype with spatially offset outlets (primary at 0°, bypass at 180°)
experiments.measurement: Apply obstruction medium covering increasing area. At each level, measure whether primary flow, bypass flow, or both are blocked. Record the coverage level at which each lumen obstructs.
experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if bypass obstructs at <75% coverage (common-mode failure too easy). PASS if bypass survives until 100% coverage (only fails when entire outlet area is covered).
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all coverage levels. Report the obstruction sequence.

experiments.name: Stagnant fluid in closed bypass lumen
experiments.hypothesis: Distal closure design drains bypass lumen completely when closed
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 2: model assumes distal closure drains lumen. Need to verify zero residual volume.
apparatus: Fluorescent dye (fluorescein, 0.01% in saline) as fluid tracer

parameters.closure_design: distal slit valve (closes at low pressure)

experiments.measurement: Fill bypass lumen with fluorescein-saline. Close valve. Wait 60s. Weigh the prototype. Then flush with clear saline and inspect under UV light for residual dye. Weigh again. Calculate residual volume by weight difference.
experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if residual volume > 0.01 mL (stagnant reservoir for bacterial growth). CONDITIONAL_FAIL if 0.001-0.01 mL (trace residual, assess antimicrobial coating). PASS if < 0.001 mL (UV-negative).
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all 5 prototypes × 3 trials. Report residual volume for each trial.

experiments.name: Primary lumen flow with bypass architecture installed
experiments.hypothesis: Concentric bypass design does not reduce primary flow by > 5%
experiments.dangerous_assumption: V20 Attack 3: model predicts 59% flow penalty if primary radius is reduced. Defense: concentric design. Need to verify concentric design actually preserves primary flow.
apparatus: Concentric dual-lumen prototype (bypass as annular sleeve)
Single-lumen control catheter (same primary radius, no bypass)
experiments.measurement: Measure primary lumen flow in concentric dual-lumen prototype vs single-lumen control at identical pressure and radius. Calculate flow penalty = (1 - Q_test / Q_control) × 100%.
experiments.failure_criterion: KILL R6 if flow penalty > 20% (chronic under-drainage during normal operation). CONDITIONAL_FAIL if 5-20% (marginal, need clinical assessment). PASS if < 5%.
experiments.stopping_rule: Test all prototypes. Report flow penalty for each pair.

pre_registration_commitment.commitment: These 7 experiments are PRE-REGISTERED. The thresholds, failure criteria, and stopping rules are FROZEN before any data is collected. Per Article VII (never weaken the verifier to rescue a claim): if results fail the pre-registered thresholds, the failure is REPORTED HONESTLY. No post-hoc threshold adjustment. No outlier exclusion. No 'the result is actually favorable if we look at it differently.' Per Article XX (problem existence gate): if the experiments show the bypass does not solve the obstruction problem (e.g., flow insufficient, valve unreliable), R6 is KILLED — not 'needs optimization.'
article_compliance: Article II: exact evidence beats semantic plausibility (measurements, not models)
Article V: fail closed but not universal rejector (if R6 passes, it passes; if it fails, it fails)
Article VII: never weaken the verifier to rescue a claim (no post-hoc threshold adjustment)
Article XV: disclose inconvenient results (report ALL data including failures)
Article XIX: never optimize for the gate (the experiment tries to KILL R6, not confirm it)
Article XX: problem existence gate (if bypass doesn't solve obstruction, R6 is killed)

summary.estimated_cost: Low — uses standard lab equipment (water column, flow meters, analytical balance). Most expensive item: 20 precision injection-molded valve prototypes (~$200-500 each = $4,000-10,000).
kill_conditions_summary: EXP-01: >1/20 valves opens outside 15-30 mmHg → KILL
EXP-03: bypass/primary ratio > 10% at normal ICP → KILL
EXP-04: bypass doesn't activate until >20% obstruction → KILL
EXP-05: bypass obstructs at <75% coverage → KILL
summary.cheapest_experiment_that_could_prove_us_: EXP-R6-01 (valve opening threshold): If the valve cannot be manufactured to open at 20-25 mmHg with <5 mmHg tolerance, R6 is dead regardless of all other findings. This is the critical-path experiment. Cost: ~$5,000 + 1 week.
